messages.subject: Re: calculating probability of detection for MCDS
parts:
Len; Thanks for the correct formula. However, unless I'm mistaken, the va=
lue for detection probability given by the corrected formula still goes neg=
ative for y>8.459 (approximately). Does one just set the detection probabi=

lity to 0 for such cases?
Eric

Sent: Saturday, July 04, 2009 7:56 PM
To: Stolen, Eric D. (KSC-DYN-301)[DYNAMAC CORP]
Cc: DISTANCE...@jiscmail.ac.uk
Subject: Re: [DIST-SAMP] calculating probability of detection for MCDS

Hi Eric (list),

There's a bug in that formula I'm afraid. I had forgotten to take the
series expansion to the forth power (2j where j is 2 in this case). The
correct formula should be

((1-exp(-(y/0.4582)^-1.195)) / (1-exp(-(0/0.4582)^-1.195)) ) *
( (1- 1.954*(y/w)^4) / (1-1.954*(0/w)^4) )

This has already been corrected in the manual for Distance 6.0, which
should see general release very soon. In the meantime, I'll send you
the revised manual chapter in a separate email. Apologies for the
confusion.

- len

messages.author: 4b4a7b00c1dd09c7
messages.subject: Re: calculating probability of detection for MCDS
parts:
Eric (list),

You're quite right, it does go to <0 at around y=8.5. My fault -- it's
a made up example and I hadn't checked. In practice, Distance should
throw an error during optimization if it found this ("Error: f(x)<0" or
some such). I've changed the example in the manual, to use real data in
one of the sample projects, so users can double-check against the plot
that they can obtain in the results. I've emailed you a draft of the
text under separate cover. Thanks for helping clarify this stuff.

- len
